title: Gus Gecko's Upside-Down Museum | Position Words for Kids

music.emotional_arrangement: pizzicato strings and glass harmonica for discovery; bass clarinet curiosity during restoration; brushed snare and celesta lift at each correct placement; elegant chamber-dance finale

voices.delivery: melodic spatial-language caper with acted character phrases; no flat narration

continuity.gus: small emerald-turquoise gecko child with orange toe pads, large amber eyes and plum velvet museum waistcoat with brass trim
continuity.mara: one dusky-lavender owl curator with round spectacles, burgundy scarf and a tiny brass key ring
continuity.museum: grand jewel-toned natural-history gallery with indigo walls, carved walnut cases, warm brass rails, patterned marble floor and four stable glowing archways
continuity.camera_rule: Architecture and floor horizon remain stable. Gus changes surface orientation; the camera performs at most one restrained orientation adjustment per scene.

scenes.action: Gus and Mara discover four displaced exhibits after a rolling display trolley stops: golden moth model, fern fossil tile, amber beetle case and moon-seed sculpture.
lyrics: Moonlight gleams through the museum hall.
Four treasures slipped from their places.
Gus says, I'll climb and help!
scenes.hero: four distinct displaced treasures beside one stopped trolley

scenes.action: Mara opens four empty display bays while Gus studies their physical brackets and plinths without labels or guessing silhouettes.
lyrics: Every treasure has a place.
Look at brackets, rails, and spaces.
Position words will guide our climb.
scenes.hero: physical mounting clues and Gus planning a safe route

scenes.action: Gus climbs a stable wall ladder and places the golden moth model above the round moonstone plinth.
lyrics: Golden wings travel up the wall.
Above means higher than the stone.
Moth shines above the moonstone.

scenes.action: Gus hangs beneath a broad shelf and slides the fern fossil tile below a tall crystal specimen.
lyrics: Gus pads softly under the shelf.
Below means lower than the crystal.
Fern rests below, snug and still.
scenes.hero: clear below relationship with stable horizon

scenes.action: Gus walks along a brass side rail and sets the amber beetle case beside a blue shell display.
lyrics: Amber beetle rides the side rail.
Beside means next to a friend.
Beetle rests beside blue shell.
scenes.hero: two exhibits side by side with visible space

scenes.action: Gus lowers the moon-seed sculpture between two carved stone birds on one long plinth.
lyrics: Moon-seed swings on safe ribbon.
Between means in the middle place.
Seed settles between two birds.
scenes.hero: one object centered between exactly two anchors

scenes.action: Mara stands behind a glass globe while Gus places a small compass in front of it, creating a readable depth pair.
lyrics: Mara waits behind the clear globe.
Compass lands in front, close by.
Behind and front make depth.
scenes.hero: one transparent globe proving front and behind

scenes.action: Gus walks the ceiling path to inspect all restored positions while Mara checks them from the floor and opens the gallery doors.
lyrics: Above, below, beside, between.
Front and behind are now placed.
Gus climbs down; doors swing wide.
scenes.hero: all relationships readable in one coherent gallery

scenes.action: Visitors enter as Gus and Mara perform a restrained chamber rhythm beneath the restored displays; Gus lands on the floor for the final pose.
lyrics: Find its place; sing the word.
Turn your view; keep clues steady.
Every treasure now feels home.

quality_requirements: Gus, Mara, all six named exhibits and the gallery architecture retain exact identity and scale.
Every spatial word is shown by physical placement before or during its exact sung phrase.
The floor horizon and at least two architectural anchors stay stable in every scene; no disorienting continuous camera roll.
This is a connected restoration caper, not a silhouette, shadow, matching-card or guessing format.
Gus has believable toe contact on wall, rail, shelf or ceiling and lands on the floor for the final pose.
Real trolley, toe, bracket, rail, ribbon, case, door and gallery effects replace spoken imitation words.
Visitors and musical-reopening staging appear only in scene 9.
All shared gates in premium-musical-video-set-2026-08-31.json pass before release.
